rubric.why: Checks that a pathway consists of linked reactions.
rubric.description: A metabolic pathway is a series of chemical reactions.
rubric.how: Award for identifying it as a series of reactions.

rubric.why: Checks that enzymes control the reactions in the pathway.
rubric.description: The reactions in a metabolic pathway are enzyme-controlled.
rubric.how: Award for stating that enzymes control or catalyse the reactions.

modelAnswer: A metabolic pathway is a series of enzyme-controlled chemical reactions that occur in a cell.
The product of one reaction may become the substrate for the next, forming intermediates before the final product.

rubric.why: Checks that denaturation changes the enzyme’s structure, including its active site.
rubric.description: Denaturation changes an enzyme’s shape and alters its active site.
rubric.how: Award for identifying a change in enzyme shape or active site.

rubric.why: Checks the effect of the structural change on enzyme action.
rubric.description: The substrate can no longer bind properly, so enzyme action is reduced or stops.
rubric.how: Award for explaining that substrate binding or enzyme action is impaired.

modelAnswer: Enzyme denaturation is a change in an enzyme’s three-dimensional shape that alters its active site.
The substrate no longer fits or binds to the altered active site, so enzyme action is reduced or stops.
